newsitem.title: JAPAN: TOKYO STOCKS REBOUND, RELIEVED BY U.S. STABILITY.
newsitem.headline: TOKYO STOCKS REBOUND, RELIEVED BY U.S. STABILITY.

text.p: Tokyo stocks recovered moderately by Tuesday midday after the previous day's nearly four percent plunge in the market benchmark, as stability in U.S. markets encouraged investors' bargain hunting, brokers said.
But although Monday's somewhat panicky sell-off was seen as excessive, concern about Japan's tenative economic recovery and about some firms' credit risks lingered, they said.
The 225-share Nikkei average ended the morning session up 191.92 points or 1.02 percent at 19,016.10, reversing Monday's slide to 18,824.18.
Its September futures stood 280 points higher at 19,060.

"After last week's sharp slides in U.S. stocks, bonds and currency, they look stabilised at least for now and that's one reason for today's recovery in Tokyo stocks," said Kazuhiro Miyake, chief strategist at Nikko Research Center.

Miyake said the Nikkei average's rise in the morning was a correction from Monday's overshooting amid thin trading volume, with leading brokerage Nomura Securities Co Ltd absent from the market due to penalties for illegal payoffs to a corporate racketeer.
"The market turned overly pessimistic about the economy yesterday," he said.
Brokers said fears that Japan's economy may not pick up soon and lingering concern about debt-laden construction companies were behind the recent decline in stocks.
"It's true that the Japanese economic recovery is slow, but it is unlikely to worsen in the future," Miyake said.

Kunihiro Hatae, general manager at Tokyo Securities Co Ltd, said: "There is still some concern about the downside risks in the Japanese market, but buying demand from investors was strong at around 19,000."
Trading volume remained modest at 163 million shares at midday, against 143 million shares traded by Monday midday.
Gainers outnumbered losers 724 to 314, while 175 issues were unchanged.
The broader TOPIX index was up 9.88 points, or 0.68 percent, at 1,469.56. The Nikkei 300 average climbed 2.08 points, or 0.73 percent, to 287.50.

In New York, the Dow industrials halted a steep two-session slide, finishing up 30.89 points, or 0.4 percent, at 8,062.11. The dollar had risen back to around 116.00 yen by Tokyo midday from 115.07/17 yen in late Tokyo on Monday.
Participants in Tokyo were still nervous about New York markets, brokers said.
"We'll watch closely to see if upcoming U.S. economic indicators show any signs of inflation. It they do and hurt U.S. stocks, that would affect Tokyo stocks," Hatae at Tokyo Securities said.
By sector, gainers were led by mining, communications, fisheries, and sea transport. The major losers were credit/lease and insurers.
